facts_zh:
Ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president freed after collapse of attempted murder case
- Published
The former wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president has been freed from remand after seven years while on trial for his attempted murder.
Marry Mubaiwa was charged in 2019, after her then husband Gen Constantino Chiwenga accused her of trying to impede his medical treatment in South Africa.
Ordering her release, a magistrate said Mubaiwa had suffered mental, physical and financial prejudice during the trial, state-owned daily the Herald said.

articles.title_zh: Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled by leopard
facts_zh:
Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled by leopard
- Published
An experienced keeper at a Dutch zoo has died days after being mauled in a leopard enclosure, the safari park has confirmed.
The woman, who had worked at Beekse Bergen park for 40 years, was caring for two Persian leopards in an indoor facility when she was attacked on Saturday.
She sustained injuries to her head and neck and had emergency surgery, but the park confirmed her death on Tuesday.

articles.title_original: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
articles.title_zh: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
facts_zh:
Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
- Published
An inquiry into the deaths of 33 detainees in Nigeria's Minna state has found they died as a result of severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and failure by officers to respond to distress calls.
Forensic and medical evidence showed the "entirely preventable" deaths had resulted from acute respiratory failure linked to prolonged confinement, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.
The evidence did not support initial claims of a disease outbreak.

all_titles.en: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds

A controversial Islamic cleric in Nigeria has been murdered outside his home in the northern state of Katsina.
Two assailants arrived on a motorcycle and shot Yahaya Masussuka in the town of Dutsin-Ma as he was saying goodbye to visitors on Monday evening, sources told the BBC.
The 47-year-old preacher and one of his guests, who was also shot, were rushed to hospital but both were pronounced dead by the attending doctor, police said.

articles.title_zh: West warns of famine risk in Sudan as civil war grinds on
facts_zh:
West warns of famine risk in Sudan as civil war grinds on
- Published
The US and 30 other Western states have warned of an "alarming deterioration" in food security in Sudan, urging the warring sides in the civil war to remove obstacles to humanitarian aid to prevent famine.
In a joint statement, the signatories said conflict was the main driver of Sudan's hunger crisis, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting food production.

"There is very little to survive on," Yusuf Roble, regional director for Islamic Relief East Africa, told BBC Newsday, describing how people returning to Omdurman were finding their homes destroyed or looted.

all_titles.en: West warns of famine risk in Sudan as civil war grinds on

facts_zh:
Co-ordinated cattle raids kill at least 72 people in South Sudan
- Published
At least 72 people have been killed during cattle raids in South Sudan's northern Warrap state, according to the regional government.
An unspecified number of cattle were taken and homes burnt during what was a "co-ordinated attack" on Monday involving two communities in Tonj North county, the state authorities said.

Such deadly violence is often part of a cycle of revenge attacks as cattle are a main source of wealth and pride for many communities and are also important as young men need them as dowries to get married.

facts_zh:
Netherlands pulls out of Eurovision again over Israel participation
- Published
The Netherlands has pulled out of next year's Eurovision Song Contest, with public broadcaster NPO citing "sensitivities" over Israel's participation - reversing a previous decision to take part.
The Netherlands and four other countries boycotted this year's event, after Dutch network Avrotros pulled out.
Avrotros said it would also not take part next year, but NPO, which oversees public broadcasting in the country, stepped in and pledged last month that the country would return in 2027.

articles.title_zh: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl half-time show
facts_zh:
Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl half-time show
- Published
Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl half-time show in February, the NFL has announced.
Jay-Z's company Roc Nation has produced the half-time show since 2019, and he plays a key role in selecting each year's performer but he has not performed before at the NFL championship game.
"Anticipation as to who Jay-Z might have guest star at halftime for the big game will now kick off," the NFL said in a statement.

articles.title_original: Chinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its toll
articles.title_zh: Chinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its toll
facts_zh: Lack of profits and the threat posed by western countries are raising concern about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boom Trillions of dollars have been wiped from China’s stock markets in recent months amid increasing anxiety about the future of artificial intelligence, as Beijing races against the United States for dominance in the sector.
The STAR 50 Index, which tracks technology and innovation companies on the Shanghai stock exchange, has plunged 40% since June.
Other indexes of major companies dropped by about 20% over the same time period.

all_titles.en: Chinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its toll
